title: Weak cobalt pricing sentiment across Antaike and LME Week
gist: Participants at the Antaike Nickel and Cobalt Forum and LME Week reported weak cobalt pricing sentiment. The causes were soft LCO demand and large Chinese stocks of sulphate, pCAM and recycled material, and Huayou, Greatpower, Tengyuan and CTT have halted metal production. Sources expect the DRC to cut export quotas by 25% next year, but Benchmark says the price response depends on how fast Chinese stocks are drawn down. European metal prices fell from $21-23/lb to $17.5-19.5/lb.

themes.theme: Oversupply and production halts in China

insights.claim: Participants at the Antaike Nickel and Cobalt Forum (13-15 October 2026) and LME Week (19-23 October 2026) uniformly reported weak cobalt pricing sentiment. They blamed soft LCO demand and large stocks of cobalt sulphate, pCAM and recycled material in China.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Minerals
insights.so_what: Near-term cobalt price upside is capped by inventory overhang, which weighs on cobalt-exposed miners and refiners.
insights.quote: This is driven by soft LCO demand and large stocks of cobalt sulphate, precursor cathode active material (pCAM) and recycled material in China.
insights.locator: Cobalt market participants at the recent

insights.claim: Chinese producers Huayou, Greatpower, Tengyuan and CTT have halted cobalt metal production, and Greatpower's salt line is running at only 20% utilisation.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Minerals
insights.so_what: Supply curtailment by Chinese refiners points to margin distress and could set a floor under prices if the cuts persist.
insights.quote: Huayou, Greatpower, Tengyuan and CTT have halted metal production, while Greatpower’s salt line is running at only 20% utilisation.
insights.locator: Cobalt market participants at the recent

insights.claim: Several market sources expect the DRC to cut cobalt export quotas by 25% next year. Some traders expect an announcement in late October or early November 2026, while others expect intervention in January or February 2027.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Minerals
insights.so_what: A DRC quota announcement is a datable catalyst for cobalt prices and DRC-exposed producers.
insights.quote: Several sources told Benchmark they expect the DRC to cut export quotas by 25% next year

insights.claim: A 25% DRC quota cut would hit a market already well supplied with intermediates, so the price response depends on how quickly Chinese stocks are drawn down.
insights.speaker: George Ingall
insights.so_what: Investors should watch Chinese inventory drawdown rather than the quota headline when timing a cobalt rally.
insights.quote: A 25% quota cut would land on a market that is already well supplied with intermediates, so the price response will depend on how quickly Chinese stocks are drawn down

insights.claim: Market participants have tempered hopes that Indonesia can fill a DRC shortfall. Expectations voiced at the events put Indonesian MHP cobalt output at 40-50kt, below the 60-70kt expected in China.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Minerals
insights.so_what: Lower Indonesian MHP output would make DRC quota cuts more price-supportive than the China consensus implies.
insights.quote: expectations voiced of Indonesian MHP output of 40–50kt rather than the 60–70kt expected in China

themes.theme: Black mass as a key cobalt feedstock

insights.claim: Chinese cobalt sulphate producers increasingly rely on recycled material. Sources say the cheapest sulphate on the market comes from black mass, and most estimates put recycled cobalt supply at 30-45kt per year.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Minerals
insights.so_what: Recycling is now a structural, low-cost supply source that dampens the price impact of disruptions to primary mining.
insights.quote: the cheapest sulphate in the market comes from black mass, with most estimates of recycled cobalt supply sitting between 30kt–45kt per year
insights.locator: Black mass emerges as key feedstock

insights.claim: During the Antaike Forum, European cobalt metal prices were $21-23/lb, well above the $16-17/lb heard in China. During LME Week the European market corrected down, with transactions heard at $17.5-19.5/lb.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Minerals
insights.so_what: The Europe-China premium is converging lower, which signals weakness spreading from China into Western markets.
insights.quote: During LME Week, the European market corrected down, with transactions heard in the range of $17.5-19.5/lb.

insights.claim: Benchmark's George Ingall argues that fragmented cobalt prices make reliable reference prices more important. Benchmark promotes its IOSCO-assured assessments, which cover hydroxide, MHP, sulphate, oxide and metal.
insights.speaker: George Ingall
insights.so_what: This is a promotional point, but it shows that cobalt price discovery is opaque and disputed.
insights.quote: With prices this fragmented, reliable reference points matter more than ever
insights.locator: Dislocation raises demand for transparent reference
